hints: Focus on two separate tests here, first whether the OH carbon is attached to two other carbons, and second what size alkene forms.
An alkene with Mr = 70 must be C5H10, since 5 x 12 + 10 x 1 = 70, so your starting alcohol must contain 5 carbons.
Now check which 5-carbon alcohol is secondary and can lose water to give that C5 alkene, remembering tertiary alcohols have three carbons on the C-OH.
walkthrough:
**Check what secondary means**

A secondary alcohol has the OH group on a carbon joined to two other carbons. A tertiary alcohol has it on a carbon joined to three other carbons.

Rule: $\text{primary: RCH}_2\text{OH, secondary: R}_2\text{CHOH, tertiary: R}_3\text{COH}$

**Work out the target alkene**

Dehydration removes $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ from an alcohol to give an alkene with the same carbon skeleton.

$$M_r(\text{alkene}) = 12n + 1(2n) = 14n = 70$$
So $n = 5$. The product must be $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$, so the alcohol must be a $\text{C}_5$ alcohol, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$.

**Classify and count each option**

Option A is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)(CH}_3)_2$, tertiary $\text{C}_5$. Option B is $\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH(OH)CH}_3$, secondary $\text{C}_5$. Option C is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, secondary $\text{C}_4$. Option D is cyclopentanol, secondary $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{11}\text{OH}$.

Only B is both secondary and $\text{C}_5$.

**Confirm the dehydration**

B, 3-methylbutan-2-ol, loses water to give methylbutene, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$.

$$\text{C}_5\text{H}_{12}\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C}_5\text{H}_{10} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$M_r = 70$ as required, so this is the answer.

options.A: This is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, a tertiary alcohol because the C-OH is bonded to three carbons. It would dehydrate to a C5 alkene with Mr = 70, but it fails the secondary alcohol test.
options.B: This is 3-methylbutan-2-ol. The C-OH is bonded to two carbons, so it is secondary, and it has 5 carbons. Dehydration gives C5H10 with Mr = 5(12) + 10(1) = 70. Both conditions are met.
options.C: This is butan-2-ol, which is secondary, but it has only 4 carbons. Its dehydration product is butene, C4H8, with Mr = 56, not 70.
options.D: Cyclopentanol is secondary, but dehydration of a cyclic alcohol gives a cycloalkene. Cyclopentene is C5H8 with Mr = 68, not 70, because the ring loses two extra hydrogens.
